clue.text: Echidna concealed by a plantation

indicators.note: concealed is read as disguised, so the letters of the animal's name and the article are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spiny anteater is hiding out somewhere on a plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no run of the clue gives the answer; here it means disguised, and the letters of ECHIDNA plus A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or farm in Spanish-speaking countries, the kind of land a plantation is.

clue.text: Bully for Hesione Hushabye's husband!

definitions.meaning: to bully is to intimidate or browbeat
in Shaw's play Heartbreak House, Hesione Hushabye is married to a man of this name

explanation.surface: Hooray for the husband of a Shaw heroine!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully for' looks like the exclamation 'bully for you'; 'Bully' is the verb and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat someone is to hector them; Shaw's character Hesione's spouse bears the same name.

clue.text: French priest clutching at his English assistant

indicators.note: clutching means the priest's title holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: A French priest grabbing hold of his English helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a clergyman who assists a parish priest, the Anglican counterpart's helper.

clue.text: Opening for gunners in Burmese formation

indicators.note: formation is read as forming the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for gunners

explanation.surface: A gap for soldiers firing guns, built into a Burmese military formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges RA (Royal Artillery) and BURMESE together. 'Opening for gunners' reads as the definition, but 'for gunners' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasure is a splayed gap in a wall or parapet through which a gun can fire.

clue.text: US call-up body is said to play, on this

indicators.note: is said means the American term is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: in the US a draft board selects men for military service

explanation.surface: The American conscription committee supposedly plays games on this.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for the board game checkers, and 'draught' sounds like 'draft'.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkers, known in Britain as draughts, is played on a chequered board of 64 squares.

clue.text: Bicycle to deliver two letters, say

definitions.meaning: a bicycle built for two riders, one behind the other
spoken out, the name means 'T and M', a pair of letters handed over together

explanation.surface: A postman's bicycle is used to drop off a couple of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns on saying the letters T and M aloud: 'T and em'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seat cycle is called this; and 'T and M' run together sound like the word, two letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Parched? Swallow cold bitter

indicators.note: swallow means the dry word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: parched means very dry, arid
C is short for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Thirsty? Down a cold glass of bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like the beer, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and harsh in taste or smell.

clue.text: Carved ornament for a canine.

definitions.meaning: a Gothic architectural motif of small pointed projections
a canine is a pointed tooth, read literally as a dog's tooth

explanation.surface: A carved decoration made for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog, but it is also the name of a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names an Early English architectural moulding, and also an eye tooth.

clue.text: Rule of one hundred is in harmony, curiously

indicators.note: curiously signals that the letters are put together in a strange new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Ruling a hundred people peacefully would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hundred' looks like a unit, but 'one' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A state with a single sovereign ruler, a king or queen, is this form of government.

clue.text: Millet, for example, uses lines appealing to the intellect

indicators.note: uses is read as takes in or contains, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: millet is a grain crop, an example of a cereal
BR, British Rail, stands for railway lines

explanation.surface: The painter Millet's work uses lines that appeal to thinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: Millet looks like the French painter, but it is the grain. BR (British Rail) is a crossword stand-in for railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cerebral engages the mind and brain rather than the emotions.

clue.text: Guardian of treasure in costume?

parts.note: drag is theatrical costume, especially clothes of the opposite sex
in, as in wearing, gives on (with a costume on)

explanation.surface: A treasure-keeper turns up dressed for a fancy-dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In costume' is read as having one's drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend a fire-breathing beast, as in Beowulf or Tolkien's Smaug, sleeps on a hoard of gold.

clue.text: Fitted hair carpet, at bishop's office

indicators.note: fitted is read as fitted together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wall-to-wall hair carpet laid in the bishop's study.
explanation.walkthrough: A patriarch is a senior bishop in the Eastern churches.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or see of a patriarch, a bishop of the highest rank.

clue.text: Porter has no trains for old Italian town

indicators.note: has no means the following piece is missing from the word for the porter

parts.note: an ostiary is a doorkeeper or porter, especially of a church
RY, railway, stands for trains

explanation.surface: A railway porter is idle in an old Italian town with no trains running.
explanation.walkthrough: An OSTIARY is a church doorkeeper, the kind of porter meant; RY (railway) comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient port of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Piano passage that completes one's education

parts.note: a grand is a large kind of piano
a tour is a journey or passage from place to place

explanation.surface: Learning a piano piece rounds off a person's schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano passage' suggests a run of music, but it splits into the instrument and a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Young gentlemen of the 18th century finished their schooling by travelling round Europe's cultural cities.

clue.text: Fat wedge of toffee

parts.note: butter is a cooking fat
a scotch is a wedge put under a wheel to stop it rolling

explanation.surface: A thick slab of chewy sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle sweet made of butter and brown sugar, a kind of toffee.

clue.text: 'One of Bennett's quintet, or just a quarter of it?

definitions.meaning: Arnold Bennett wrote about the Five Towns of the Potteries, where china is made
a district of a city where Chinese people live

explanation.surface: Is one of Arnold Bennett's five towns just a district of it?
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's novels are set in the Five Towns of the Potteries, the china-making area of Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A Potteries pottery-making town is a china town; a Chinese district of a city is a quarter.

clue.text: One of three fired, retired and gone to pieces

parts.note: abed means in bed, having retired for the night

indicators.note: gone to pieces means the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: One of three workers was sacked, withdrew and fell apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests sacking; it refers to the Book of Daniel, where three men were thrown into the fiery furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadrach, Meshach and this companion survived Nebuchadnezzar's furnace in the Book of Daniel.

clue.text: It's a minor inconvenience if you have to run about a little

indicators.note: about means the word for running goes around the other piece

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: It's only a small bother if you have to jog around for a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A BIT inside FLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small trivial annoyance is likened to the slight itch of an insect's bite.

clue.text: An enthusiasm that possesses the Dervishes?

definitions.text: An enthusiasm that possesses the Dervishes?

parts.words: An enthusiasm that possesses the Dervishes?
parts.note: whirling dervishes spin in a religious dance, so their passion is pictured as a mania for ballet

explanation.surface: Some craze has taken hold of the whirling Sufi dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a passionate love of ballet, which the dancing dervishes are humorously credited with.

clue.text: Jeu d'esprit, eg, featuring a peri

indicators.note: featuring means the letters appear within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A witty piece of writing, for instance, starring a Persian fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or elf in Persian folklore, a supernatural spirit.

clue.text: The Famous Five were attracted to it

definitions.text: The Famous Five were attracted to it

parts.words: The Famous Five were attracted to it
parts.note: Harry Wharton's Famous Five of Greyfriars appeared in a boys' weekly paper, and also something that attracts things

explanation.surface: Enid Blyton's young adventurers were drawn to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Famous Five looks like Enid Blyton's children, but here they are Frank Richards's Greyfriars schoolboys, whose stories ran in a boys' weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of iron that pulls metal towards it; also the title of the old story paper featuring Billy Bunter's schoolmates.

clue.text: Assistant backs decimal system to do with Circle Line

indicators.note: backs means the word for the helper is turned round

parts.note: aid is help, or an assistant
the metric system counts in tens

explanation.surface: A helper supports decimalisation on the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns AID to DIA. The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here it is the diameter, a line across a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Diametric relates to a diameter, the straight line through the middle of a circle.

clue.text: Unavoidable absence of a remittance man

definitions.meaning: enforced time away from one's country
a man living abroad on money sent from home, often to keep him away

explanation.surface: A man sent abroad on an allowance has no choice but to stay away.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment from one's homeland, or a person who lives in such banishment.

clue.text: Every character lost bet for a start

indicators.note: lost means the named word drops out of the longer one

parts.note: every letter or character together makes the alphabet

explanation.surface: Everyone in the story lost their wager right at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, stands for a beginning, as in 'alpha and omega'.

clue.text: Boy doesn't begin to get one right solution

indicators.note: doesn't begin means the boy's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Felix is a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A schoolboy can't even start working out the correct answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't begin' takes the F off FELIX, leaving ELIX.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal liquid, a preparation dissolved in alcohol or syrup.

clue.text: Winner of the Dunmow Flitch — a kind of philosopher?

definitions.meaning: the Dunmow Flitch is an Essex custom awarding a side of bacon to a married couple who have not quarrelled for a year, so the winner is jokingly one who brings home the bacon
a follower of the philosopher Francis Bacon

explanation.surface: Is the couple who take the bacon prize also a sort of thinker?
explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch is an old Essex prize of a side of bacon for a married couple who have gone a year without a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names followers of Francis Bacon's thought; whimsically, it also fits someone who won a bacon prize.

clue.text: Its constituents have to be broken

definitions.text: Its constituents have to be broken

parts.words: Its constituents have to be broken
parts.note: the saying goes that this dish cannot be made without cracking eggs

explanation.surface: A thing whose parts must be smashed before it exists.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg dish whose ingredients must be cracked open first, as the proverb about eggs says.

clue.text: Find note in waistcoat to buy more shares.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: Discover a banknote in a waistcoat pocket and put it into more stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' here is a musical note, not a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvest is to put returns back into further holdings or stock.
